title: 3.5: NFT Metadata Generator: On-Chain SVG & JSON

steps.description: In this short tour you will see how `NFTMetadataGenerator` builds on-chain images, JSON metadata, and full `tokenURIs`, and how the `Position-NFT` contracts lean on it.
The three hard-coded SVG colour constants that every Position-NFT artwork shares:

- `SVG_BG_COLOR` = `#d4c3b7` (sand background)
- `SVG_TEXT_COLOR` = `#0a3a60` (dark blue text)
- `SVG_ACCENT_COLOR` = `#0a3a60` (dark blue accents)
These values are later interpolated into the generated SVG.
generateSVG() assembles an SVG image with abi.encodePacked.  Notice how the caller-supplied `title` (l.32) and the numeric `tokenId` (l.40) are embedded directly.
The function returns a single string that already contains the full **<svg>** document. Because `abi.encodePacked` concatenates bytes, no external storage or loops are needed.

generateJSONString() wraps the SVG in ERC-721 compatible JSON:
- name  -> "AlchemistV3 Position #<id>" (l.56-58)
- description -> static human text (l.59)
- image -> an in-place data: URI that contains the Base64-encoded SVG (l.60-62)
The entire JSON blob is itself Base64-encoded (l.54).
`generateTokenURI()` glues everything together; it calls the previous helpers and prefixes the result with the `data:application/json;base64,` scheme.

Whenever an NFT marketplace or wallet asks either `Position-NFT` contract for `tokenURI`, the call is routed to `NFTMetadataGenerator`. This keeps metadata fully on-chain, ensures a uniform styling via the three colour constants, and avoids duplicating logic across contracts.
